competitive_landscape: Inter-island transport is dominated by Air Tahiti, with diesel ferries only on the Papeete-Moorea channel and slow resort tenders elsewhere. There is essentially no fast premium water network between the islands — a genuinely greenfield, high-margin opening where foiling both diversifies away from single-airline dependence and creates a signature luxury experience.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core lagoon and inter-island legs — Papeete↔Moorea (~12 nm), Bora Bora lagoon transfers (~4 nm), Raiatea↔Taha'a↔Bora Bora (~22 nm) — sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on calm, reef-protected lagoon water, the ideal foiling environment, in a market with almost no fast water competition.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Unlocks the marquee long line-hauls — Tahiti↔Bora Bora (~140 nm) and onward to the Tuamotus — as premium experiential cruises beyond the all-electric range, with no charging dependency on remote motus.

regulatory_note: French Polynesia is an overseas collectivity of France with its own maritime administration; vessels operate under French/EU-aligned safety frameworks. The territorial government actively promotes sustainable tourism, favouring zero-emission marine transport as a brand and environmental fit for its lagoon ecosystems.
seasonality: The dry season (May-October) is peak, with a warmer wetter season November-April; the lagoons stay largely protected year-round, and the luxury resort demand is relatively season-resilient given long-haul booking patterns.
summary: French Polynesia's Society Islands — Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Raiatea, Taha'a, Huahine — are the global archetype of luxury island-hopping: turquoise lagoons, overwater bungalows (Four Seasons, St Regis, Conrad, InterContinental) and a visitor economy built on seclusion and privacy. Yet inter-island travel depends overwhelmingly on Air Tahiti's flight network, with very little fast premium water transport between islands; the lagoons themselves are calm, protected and almost purpose-shaped for Pioneer II. With ~326,000 international visitors in 2024 and a government pushing tourism growth and sustainability, this is a greenfield, high-margin market where a silent foiling shuttle would both relieve dependence on a single airline and deliver a signature on-water luxury experience.
tagline: The most iconic luxury lagoon on earth, a string of overwater-bungalow islands, and almost no fast inter-island water link. Greenfield, premium, and made for foiling.
